chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ṣafwān, from one who narrated it, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If the muḥṣan fornicator confesses, the Imam is the first to stone him, then the people. But if the evidence is established against him, the evidence-bearers are the first to stone him, then the Imam, then the people.

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: he confessed or admitted the offense
key_terms.الزَّانِي: the fornicator or adulterer subject to the ruling mentioned here
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the legitimate authority who carries out the prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: the legally valid evidence or testimony by which the charge is established
key_terms.الْمُحْصَنُ: one who is muḥṣan, meaning legally protected by marriage status in the context of hadd rulings
key_terms.يَرْجُمُهُ: he stones him, referring to initiating the rajm punishment

ai.seo_question: Who begins the rajm punishment in Shia hadith when zina is proven by confession or by evidence?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the order of those who initiate the rajm punishment for a muḥṣan adulterer. It distinguishes between a case established by confession and a case established by bayyinah, assigning a different order of participation in each circumstance.
